---
title: "Run Operations and Read-only Benchmark"
subtitle: "Execute with JAX or Julia, then inspect actual recorded work"
---

**Status:** 1.0.0a2 Alpha `CONVERGING` candidate. This guide describes the current
implementation contract, not completed performance or numerical acceptance.
Historical dev10 comparison records keep their original runtime identities.

## Configure once, execute normal operations

Python 3.12 is required. The base installation supplies the pinned CPU JAX,
jaxlib and CMA dependencies. JAX executes in the calling Python process and
never discovers, preflights or invokes Julia.

Set the CPU pool before the first JAX operation:

```python
from scnsim import CircuitRun, configure_runtime

configure_runtime(cpu_threads=1)
run = CircuitRun(plan=plan, workspace="workspaces/analysis")
result = run.solve(run.original, direct_spec)
root = run.evaluate(run.original, root_spec)
```

The Run defaults to `backend="jax", precision="float64"`. Per-call omitted
backend/precision inherit the Run declaration; explicit values override it:

```python
result32 = run.solve(run.original, direct_spec, precision="float32")
result64 = run.solve(run.original, direct_spec, precision="float64")
```

Float32 selects real Float32/Complex64 kernel arrays; Float64 selects
Float64/Complex128. Host SI values and CMA state remain binary64. These are
different recorded requests, not converted views of one computed result.
Existing numerical procedures use the selected dtype's epsilon/stagnation
behavior, without a new accuracy or convergence threshold.

`configure_runtime(cpu_threads=None)` leaves the process default resource
policy. Positive integer declarations use `PJRT_NPROC` before initialization,
without altering affinity or global JAX precision/platform settings. Repeating
a known configuration is idempotent; changing initialized resources requires a
Kernel restart. An externally initialized pool's unknown size is not invented.

For JAX Optimization, an integer also declares the task CPU budget for a
persistent objective-worker pool within each generation. `None` keeps serial
execution with the existing environment, and 1 is serial. A fair gate gives
JAX work exclusive access and shares capacity among native sparse tasks.
For integer declarations, managed BLAS1 in the coordinator and workers remains
in force until workers join,
then prior limits are restored. CMA, numerical-cache registration, storage and
callbacks remain coordinator-owned; no next-generation work runs ahead.
Generation population wall time and its per-population average describe this
parallel work; the average is not an individual candidate latency.

Direct S/Y/Z, diagonal and operator-element roots, hybridized poles, S/Y/Z
transfer zeros, residue-normalized coupling and loaded operators support JAX
original, retained and transformed Views. Existing scalar selectors also serve
Optimization; loaded operators remain matrix outputs. HB requires explicit Julia:

```python
native = run.solve(run.original, hb_spec, backend="julia", precision="float64")
```

Install `scnsim[julia]` and manually provide Julia 1.12.6 on PATH or
`PYTHON_JULIAPKG_EXE`. Missing support gives an actionable feature-specific error;
there is no automatic acquisition or backend fallback. Explicit Julia compiler preflight and compiled schematics also require Julia.
`run.explain(ref, spec, *, parameters=None, backend=None, precision=None)` inherits
the Run defaults, with per-call overrides. Its JAX route lowers the captured
Plan and realizes the selected View and every Optimization objective View using
the sparse Python compiler. It returns actual axes, sparse coefficient records,
line grids and leaf evidence without initializing JAX, solving, creating an
attempt or discovering Julia. Host SI lowering remains binary64; the declared
execution precision is bound in the request, not a claim that a kernel ran.
This backend-aware explanation is `CONVERGING`. See
[Julia runtime preparation](../implementation/julia-runtime-preparation.qmd).

## Present a saved scalar Quantity

For a returned scalar root, pole, zero, response or coupling, `show()` returns
HTML and `plot()` returns a detached Plotly Figure:

```python
root.show()                   # compact Quantity / Value / Unit tables
root.show(detailed=True)      # include provenance and original stored values
root.plot(detailed=True)      # grouped Figure tables; no calculation
```

Complex components share an engineering unit and scale. The display preserves
small nonzero components and does not recompute numerical values. This scalar
presentation is `CONVERGING`; the
[presentation contract](../implementation/results-reports-and-diagrams.qmd#scalar-quantity-presentation)
defines its ownership and formatting. Operation Benchmark, matrix, sweep and
Optimization presentations retain their existing interfaces.

## Optimization and recovery

Before repeated JAX requests, `run.warmup(view, spec, parameters=None)` can
prepare the baseline topology/View and executable signatures without solving or
saving a successful result. Exact signatures can be reused; unknown future
shapes still prepare lazily. The immutable summary describes preparation only.

Optimization display defaults to `progress=True`; set `progress=False` for a
quiet call. The transient display reports completed versus committed
generations independently of `on_progress`. JAX can show each completed tell
before a commit; explicit Julia uses its existing native notification boundaries.
The `population_evaluating` display phase starts before ask; it does not announce
a completed generation or invoke the durable callback.
Display errors warn and disable the
display; durable callback errors retain their normal failure behavior.

Normal `run.optimize(...)` uses generation checkpoints and boundary diagnostics.
JAX Optimization commits every 10 completed generations by default:

```python
best = run.optimize(run.original, optimization_spec, checkpoint="generation",
                    commit_every_generations=10)
```

JAX baseline and sealed anchors are prepared in memory before candidate work;
workers acknowledge installing them without a storage transaction. Completed
generation evidence is ordered; each group publishes atomically. Generation
checkpointing additionally publishes its latest full CMA/RNG restore state. `commit_every_generations=N` accepts a positive integer excluding
booleans; `None` is invalid. Omission selects 10 for JAX and retains 1 for
explicit Julia. Explicit Julia intervals other than 1 fail before launch.
The baseline is not independently committed. The first completed group stores
its necessary baseline body once, and every N complete post-tell generations
commit together. There is no generation-0 checkpoint or initial callback;
checkpoints bind the latest completed post-tell state at generation 1 or later.
Required group ACK precedes its one callback; optional timing is separate.
Native Julia retains its existing baseline protocol. A normal or handleable-error
JAX tail flushes a shorter complete group. Larger N leaves more evidence uncommitted in Workspace-bound operation-local
scratch (mode `0700`) and can require recomputing
uncommitted generations after process death. `checkpoint="off"` omits
restore-only snapshots/anchor state while preserving the required baseline body,
complete ordered numerical observations and final result. A failed or uncertain
required group is not resent; original failure ownership remains unchanged.
Checkpoint policy and commit interval do not change the
numerical request hash; a completed result can resolve under either policy.
A cache-hit operation records requested policy and actual checkpoint availability
without manufacturing missing snapshots.
The cache and staged writer hold light body references; each committed group is
streamed atomically one body at a time. Verified resume hydration also consumes
one block at a time. Scratch is not a checkpoint, and the full ordered typed
public result ledger remains available after return.

`resume_from` accepts an exact stored checkpoint reference from the same
operation/task identity, generation policy and commit interval. An off-policy interrupted request
has no resumable state. Resume verifies identities and committed references;
it does not migrate old source state. Standalone root anchors are not CMA
checkpoints. A generation callback is notified once per commit, using its latest
committed generation, after durability acknowledgement and outside locks.
Intermediate generations do not receive deferred callbacks; callback exceptions
and KeyboardInterrupt keep their ownership.
An unflushed hard-kill diagnostic tail remains unknown.

Retrieve a committed reference through the public read-only record, selecting the
operation you intend to resume:

```python
operation = run.benchmark(operations=operation_id).document()["operations"][0]
checkpoint_ref = operation["details"]["checkpoint"]
best = run.optimize(run.original, optimization_spec,
                    checkpoint="generation", commit_every_generations=10,
                    resume_from=checkpoint_ref)
```

`operation_id` comes from the `operations` rows returned by `run.benchmark()`.
`details.checkpoint` is the latest committed snapshot for that operation's
actual attempt, or its exact resume source when no newer snapshot exists;
`details.checkpoint_attempt_id` identifies its owning attempt. A cache-hit row
references the selected success's actual checkpoint. This read projection also
reconstructs committed state after a hard kill without requiring a finished
operation row. An interrupted `checkpoint="off"` operation has no resumable
reference. Pass the complete public reference unchanged; do not reconstruct its
checkpoint or ownership fields.
For current SQLite records, content references use `schema_version=3`,
`storage="sqlite"`, `database="operations.sqlite3"`, `role`, `byte_length` and
`sha256`. The hash binds canonical object bytes, not the mutable database file.
Pass the public reference unchanged; historical file references remain readonly.
No private storage import or manual checkpoint reconstruction is needed.
Use the same commit interval when resuming.

Current JAX operation evidence lives in the bound Plan leaf’s
`operations/operations.sqlite3`, using DELETE journaling and EXTRA synchronization.
Readonly `resolve`, Benchmark and `BenchmarkResult.open` do not create, migrate
or repair a database. If they raise `WorkspaceRecoveryRequiredError`, explicitly
call `run.recover_workspace()` on the bound Run, then retry the readonly operation.
Recovery is limited to that leaf; an absent database in a valid leaf is a no-op.
Preserve the whole leaf, including any journal, when relocating it. Content
references remain relative to its database and are not rewritten. This is not a
physical power-loss guarantee. Explicit Julia retains its native storage and
verification contract.

## Read operation evidence

```python
from scnsim import BenchmarkResult

record = run.benchmark()
reopened = BenchmarkResult.open(record.workspace)
optimization_record = run.benchmark(method="optimize", backend="jax")
html = record.to_html()
record.write_html("operation-history.html")
```

`run.benchmark(*, operations=None, method=None, backend=None, precision=None,
status=None)` reads the current Plan leaf. It does not accept a Spec, launch
another calculation, initialize JAX, choose a comparison arm or mutate records.
`BenchmarkResult.workspace` is the exact operation-store directory containing
`operations.sqlite3` (`<Plan leaf>/operations`), not the enclosing Workspace root.
`BenchmarkResult.open(record.workspace)` reopens that same store read-only; it
does not discover a leaf, scan the enclosing root or perform recovery. Reopening
reads that store's recorded operations; filters on the original `run.benchmark()`
call are not persisted as a new store.
`run.resolve(...)` is likewise read-only and selects the exact verified numerical
request using the Run defaults or explicit backend/precision overrides.

A returned ParameterSweepResult may contain both successful and failed points.
The operation status describes whether the public call completed; per-point
statuses describe numerical outcomes. A completed sweep is not a claim that all
points succeeded. Single-point numerical failures still raise typed errors.

The timeline shows operation roots below their actual child details, with zoom,
collapse, cursor inspection, counts and filters. It distinguishes compilation
from verified result reuse and references ordered numerical evidence without
copying candidate histories. One numerical batch owns one measured interval;
there are no invented per-candidate timings. JAX intervals synchronize actual
work before closing. Parent intervals are inclusive and overlapping, so nested
durations must not be summed. Cumulative operation duration differs from wall
span. Unaligned historical clocks and unknown timings remain explicit.

The root begins at the method's first clock read. Its interval includes final
Plan-lock acquisition, Plan revalidation and pending-span archival through the
root endpoint; these costs have no separate named phase row. Only the final root append and
return tail remain outside that endpoint. Read-only resolve and Benchmark do not
persist operation roots or recursive self-spans. Partial records retain actual
failure/interruption state and numerical references; `operation["details"]["failure"]`
exposes the exact saved failure when present. They do not acquire a fabricated
winner or terminal result.

For explicit Julia operations, trace references point to the native verified
request, canonical attempt, receipt and result. Native `attempt_id` is the actual
canonical attempt SHA, including when an existing result is reused; it does not
claim a new launch. Native task/environment IDs remain null, with available
native environment facts in `details.native_environment`. A failed operation
retains the request and any verified numerical evidence actually available;
missing results and unaligned native clocks remain explicit.

## Historical comparison records

The old public comparison executor and its arm declarations are superseded.
Historical files retain their original wheel/backend/precision/clock identities;
current readers reject older operation Workspaces. Create a new v6 Workspace and
recompute for current readback. Historical files are neither migrated nor deleted.
Read-only opening applies to the explicit current v6 operation-store locator:

```python
from scnsim import BenchmarkResult
benchmark = run.benchmark()
report = BenchmarkResult.open(benchmark.workspace)
```

Native Julia result files retain their separate native ownership and readback
contract. No GPU, automatic mesh choice, new CMA algorithm or
numerical/performance acceptance condition is introduced.
